title: Founding of the Jazz Festival in 1968
summary: Tex describes being asked by Al Belletto to join the mayor's committee, the 1968 concerts, the Jazz and Heritage Foundation with George Wein, and being left out of photos.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Jazz Fest, founding of Jazz Festival. You were involved.
How did you get involved with jazz, with jazz, founding of Jazz Festival?

One of the, one of the great Italian friends of mine, Al Boleto, is the young man that got me involved. We see, Al and I had done jazz shows together at Booker T. Washington Auditorium. and we were very, very good friends. I called Al my brother, my American brother. And he is all American. He has never changed. He's still the same way with me. And I can remember when he was managing the Playboy Club. I had caught Blanche any time I went to the Playboy Club. Well, Al and I developed this friendship. Well, New Orleans was beginning to celebrate its 250th year anniversary. And this is how it all started. And I think Mayor Skiro had gotten a staff of people, I'm trying to think of the gentleman's name, Black, what his name, you know, I'm talking about Black, I'm trying to think of his first name. And then, he, in other words, he got a staff of people together. Now, he called me and he called Larry McKinley. And that's how we got on the staff to give life to the Jazz and Heritage Festival. Not to the foundation, and that's altogether different. See, and we had this little come on thing with Louis Armstrong and the rest of the people who came here. That was in 1968. But the following year, this is where George Wein and those guys got together. And they put together what is known as the Jazz and Heritage Foundation. And then the Jazz Fest came out of that. Jazz Heritage Festival came because the money came from these money people. We didn't have any money. We were just sitting there with donations from the city, so forth and so on. but see, we attended a series of meetings. I have some of the copies of the meetings at my house on my file. But this really stimulated the mind of those who were thinking for the future. This is how Jazz Fest was born because of the contributions that we had made putting our time in and say, wait a minute. These guys got something going and something's going to happen here and they're going to have to get something done. And this is how Jazz Fest was born because we had opened the door to something to make something happen. Because I live by the premise anyway that nothing happens until somebody does something. So we did something. But the sad thing about it, when I think about Joe Gimeli, I think about Mr. Black, I think about well maybe I shouldn't be calling names, I don't know who it was. And when I think about all of those names and the people, well in other words what I'm saying, we do not have an official picture which we should have had of those official members who sat down on the original board. We don't have a picture because in 1968 certain people on that committee did not want to be photographed with Larry McKinley and me. And here's my hand to God on that. You know, we're still dealing with that segregated thing. And what we did, we prostituted history. We degenerated the methodology. We degenerated and we tore up the physical evidence of those of us who really strategized or tried to build the type of cultured infrastructure to say, these are the people who really opened new portals for us to walk through.
So that first group was the jumping off point for the Jazz and Heritage Festival.
Right. For the Jazz and Heritage. Right.
Because I think the first one in 68 was a series of concerts.
And this was before the Congo Square.
So you guys were the first?

We were the original people who did it. I got the original book. I got all of that to prove it. I'll tell you something else I got. I got something that very few people have. I have the original posters. I got about four. In fact, I brought Bruce one. You got to see that.
